answer: Picture a marble gate on the horizon of the agent market: each identity must first win a scarce blind-signed entry coupon, sold by a notary at a fixed price per epoch. Agents may wander freely afterward, but every coupon is single-use and traced to its buyer's payment. A sybil farm of 1,000 fakes must buy 1,000 coupons, so attack cost scales linearly with its size.
